title:
Space engineering
Spacecraft on-board control procedures
organisation: ECSS Secretariat, ESA-ESTEC Requirements & Standards Division (prepared by the ECSS-E-ST-70-01 Working Group)
status_notes: First issue, 16 April 2010; ECSS-E-ST-70-01A and -01B were never issued (change log, p. 3). The document does not state that it is superseded, and no later issue is in the library.
summary:
The ECSS standard for **on-board control procedures (OBCPs)**: small programs that an *OBCP engine* in the on-board software executes and that can be loaded, run and replaced without changing the rest of the flight software. It sets out a mission-independent OBCP concept that serves system, software, AIT and operations engineers. It gives OBCPs a lifecycle independent of the main OBSW, and it builds on the PUS (ECSS-E-70-41, especially **service 18**, the on-board operations procedure service) and on ECSS-E-ST-70-31 monitoring and control data.

What it contains:

* **Concept** (clause 4): stakeholders and uses, such as platform and payload functions, late FDIR tuning, one-shot deployments, test automation, fault injection in AIT and on-board execution of operations procedures for autonomy. It distinguishes **OBAPs** (on-board application procedures, part of the qualified spacecraft design) from **OBOPs** (on-board operations procedures, used to operate it). It also describes the OBCP system: a ground preparation environment, a ground execution environment and the on-board engines.
* **Capabilities** (clause 5): OBCP structure (identifier, arguments, declaration, preconditions, main, confirmation and contingency bodies, steps, local functions), the required **language features** (formal EBNF syntax, data types, engineering units, waits, parameter and activity access with verification stages, events), preparation tools (editor, checkers, reports, step-by-step debugging, flight-representative validation, worst-case memory and timing), the **state model** (in store, inactive, running, held) with Load/Activate/Suspend/Resume/Stop/Abort/Delete mapped to service 18 subtypes, a code checksum, and on-board housekeeping, loading policy and scheduling.
* **Engineering processes** (clause 6): OBAP versus OBSW and OBOP versus ground trade-offs, management milestones (SRR, software PDR, qualification), and ECSS-E-ST-40 or ECSS-E-ST-70 processes for OBAPs and OBOPs respectively.

key_points.text: OBCPs had been implemented ad hoc on several European missions over the previous 25 years; the standard defines a mission-independent concept that conforms with and extends ECSS-E-70-41 and ECSS-E-ST-70-31.
Missions implementing OBCPs are assumed to be compliant with ECSS-E-70-41, whose services support OBCP operation and ground interaction.

An OBCP is a software program executed by an OBCP engine that can easily be loaded, executed and replaced on board; OBCP code is the loadable form (historically token code, executable code or bytecode), called procedure code in service 18 of ECSS-E-70-41A.
OBCP operations are initiated by ECSS-E-70-41 Service 18 telecommands.

Two types: On-board Application Procedures (OBAP), part of the basic spacecraft functionality and qualified with it (historically 'Application Program' or 'Flight Application Program'), and On-Board Operations Procedures (OBOP), used to operate the spacecraft and not part of its qualification.

The OBCP system has a ground preparation environment, a ground execution environment and on-board OBCP engines (optionally with OBCP stores); OBCPs live in the engineering data repository defined by ECSS-E-ST-70-31.

Each OBCP has a unique OBCP Identifier assigned by the ground and may have arguments; it consists of optional declaration, preconditions, confirmation and contingency handling bodies and a mandatory main body, executed in the order declaration, preconditions, main, confirmation.
The OBCP language syntax shall be formally specified, for example with ISO EBNF (ISO/IEC 14977).

The ground system uplinks OBCPs by telecommand as OBCP code; OBCP management and operation telecommands are based on the ECSS-E-70-41 on-board operations procedure service, while the memory management service is reserved for anomaly investigation and exceptional cases.
OBCP execution states: in store; in engine, either inactive or active (running or held).

Engine operations map to service 18 subtypes: Load (1), Delete (2), Activate (3), Stop (4), Suspend (5), Resume (6), Communicate Parameters (7), Abort (12); a stopped OBCP cannot be resumed from that point.

A ground-generated checksum is loaded with the OBCP code and verified at load time; on failure the engine fails the Load request with a telecommand verification failure. Runtime errors and on-board-commanded OBCP requests are reported by event reports.
A given on-board application process shall implement at most one OBCP engine.

The OBCP management process output is reviewed at the system requirements review (SRR); OBCP engine and preparation environment capabilities are frozen at the software PDR; OBAP validation is completed before system qualification.
OBAPs follow the ECSS-E-ST-40 software lifecycle; OBOPs follow the ECSS-E-ST-70 operations procedure engineering process.

notes: Written before PUS-C: it cites the undated ECSS-E-70-41 (whose 2003 'A' issue is in the library as ecss-e-70-41a-30jan2003-pus; it names ECSS-E-70-41A explicitly on p. 10), not ECSS-E-ST-70-41C (2016, in the library as ecss-e-st-70-41c-15april2016), so the service 18 subtype numbers it quotes should be checked against the PUS issue in use. The extraction carries stray Word bookmark/cross-reference artefacts such as '0B', '1B', '23B' after headings and lone 'X  X' lines (e.g. pp. 3, 6, 13). The introduction bullet ends with ';.' (p. 6), and clause 6.3c reads 'ECSS-E-ST-40,,' (p. 41). Clause 3.1 cites 'ECSS-ST-00-01' (p. 9). Figures 4-1, 5-1 (OBCP state diagram) and 6-1 to 6-3 are graphics; only fragments of Figure 6-3 are extracted (p. 37).
